summary: User asked what the "Kaia Notes Added" Coaching Metrics column tracks now that notes were removed from the Kaia UI; team acknowledged a reporting gap and discussed switching the metric to count comments instead, which customers have also requested.

Asked why the "add Kaia to meeting" button was greyed out for a user at ITA Group; resolved as expected behavior since recording consent/compliance was enabled, which forces the consent flow and disables manual add.

Requested review of a stale Jira about AI meeting summaries being blocked by Azure OpenAI content-filter false positives; engineering confirmed the issue is a strict/non-deterministic content filter, regenerated the affected summaries, and rolled out custom (looser) content filters on gpt-4.1 deployments to reduce future false-positive blocks.

Shared an internal tip/workaround: for Zoom meetings you scheduled but don't attend, adding an alternate host in Outlook lets that host allow Kaia to join and record, since Kaia normally can't record without a host present.

Asked whether the Kaia in-call companion screen for Alter Domus (Teams) could be customized/branded like a competitor's; official answer was no out-of-the-box support, though team explored whether a Teams admin could manually swap the app manifest/logo.
/kaiaq bot question confirming Amplify is required to use/leverage coach card auto-scoring.
/kaiaq bot question asking if the Gong-Outreach API integration is still supported; confirmed yes, it relies on APIv2.
Asked why AI Topics Explorer profile setting was/wasn't visible for a Lyft admin despite the checkbox being present; resolved as the feature requiring an Amplify license, which Lyft does not have.
Requester asked for a status update on an open Jira feature request (VI-14532).

Relayed a prospect's (unnamed fin-serv company) compliance question about recording with Kaia and keeping the summary while not retaining the transcript; team explained short retention windows and seller-side-only recording as possible options.

Reported the Kaia companion window bookmark button greyed out and call timer frozen at 0:00 on two separate prod calls; engineering suspected stale meeting-start-time data in the Zoom nested view but could not reproduce or confirm a fix.

SailPoint users were receiving repeated (multiple per hour) Kaia licensing/auth-required emails during their license migration; traced to license-change events firing the reminder email repeatedly, which continued/worsened even after migration completed and had no customer-facing disable option.

Motive asked for org-level (not user-level) controls to restrict Kaia auto-join to external-only calls, plus reporting on individual auto-join setting changes; confirmed as a valid feature request with no current reporting capability available.

SailPoint appeared to be missing the "web conference apps" card in Kaia personal settings after license migration; resolved as expected behavior since the provider cards are intentionally hidden while an admin is impersonating a user.
Asked whether Verified Caller ID would be expanded beyond US numbers for a large (unnamed) expansion opportunity; redirected to the correct channel (#vxp) with no substantive answer given here.
Minitab (Teams) asked whether recordings can show all meeting participants instead of only the active speaker.
Confirmed that content cards appear for live sessions on Google Meet (not Google Voice as originally worded).
Reported an error uploading a Zoom recording into Kaia; team checked license type and error logs (found none), and the issue self-resolved on retry.

SailPoint reported internal 1:1 meetings being auto-recorded by Kaia and visible to all employees; confirmed there is no org-wide setting to exclude internal meetings from auto-join (only per-user), so a feature request was submitted on the customer's behalf.
Requested that a shareable Kaia recording link be auto-generated and auto-populated into the follow-up email, instead of manually creating and adding the link each time; logged as a feature request.

Kpler had a content card stuck in "Processing" state since 5/21; engineering traced it to an orphaned/out-of-sync Azure search index entry, manually deleted the stale card, and asked the customer to recreate it if still needed.
Asked whether the Kaia user-level auto-join setting allowing "anyone outside your organization" had been removed; confirmed it has not been removed.

SingleStore's content cards had never popped up on meetings despite being created; explained that trigger words alone aren't enough and need surrounding intent context (e.g. naming the competitor product) to fire.

Motive's content cards (Thermo King, Fleetio) weren't firing; diagnosed as misconfiguration where intent words were used as product/trigger names instead of pairing integration-intent phrasing with actual product names.

An enterprise new-logo prospect wanted to force more virtual meetings to be auto-recorded with exclusions for certain cases; received a detailed breakdown of current auto-join/auto-record capabilities and limitations by conferencing provider, plus compliance/consent considerations.

An unnamed customer wanted to run Kaia without call transcripts (summary only) and a per-call 24-hour deletion option rather than org-wide retention; closest existing option is one-sided recording for voice calls, and a feature request was recommended for the per-call deletion ask.

Noted that Kaia coach card auto-scoring always targets the meeting host, which breaks coaching workflows when the SC/SDR (not the host) is who should be scored; PM and others agreed it's a valid enhancement to target scoring by role/team/specific users.
Asked if there's a hard time limit for Kaia on WebEx calls; answered that Kaia has an 8-hour max but also exits based on inactivity/no-speaker rules and participant join/leave timing.

Asked what notifications are sent after an uploaded file finishes processing in Kaia (upload complete, summary ready, in-app/email); answered that uploaded files get the same notifications as regular meetings.
/kaiaq bot question confirming that edits to a Kaia summary save for everyone with access, not just the editor's own view, with a pointer to the recording visibility/privacy settings.

Asked whether the transcript with minute marks is viewable for post-call ingested (uploaded) recordings; confirmed yes, and user discovered a newly added "Recording source" filter from last quarter's release.

/kaiaq bot question on whether sub-pages are needed to train Kaia's vocabulary or just the homepage URL; answered the root link plus reachable linked pages is sufficient, and noted content cards and the org vocabulary settings page are the other ways Kaia learns terms.

Asked via /kaiaq what happens when the data retention checkbox for meetings is disabled; bot explained recordings then persist indefinitely unless manually deleted, since the time-based retention policy is turned off.

Investigated why a compete content card wasn't firing despite trigger keywords appearing in a memsql call; resolved as expected behavior since trigger words must occur within about 30 seconds of each other.

Asked how Medius Software can disable RSC mode so Kaia can join meetings where the user isn't host; guided to the meeting-provider reconnect flow, with a caveat that customer-hosted external calls would still be blocked.
Routeware's Kaia is failing to auto-join Zoom meetings with a Datadog 'Anonymous User' error despite reconnecting Zoom.

Asked via /kaiaq where the Kaia live window appears in the Teams app; bot said it should pop out for live transcription, but the user reported the pop-up appeared with transcription not working, and the thread ended without a resolution.
Asked whether this channel was the right place to submit AI auto-scoring feedback; confirmed yes, for coaching auto-scoring feedback.

Asked why a 15-second in-person recording took ~20 minutes to process; engineering traced it to the transcription retry/backoff schedule being poorly tuned for very short calls and committed to a fix to cut delays for short recordings.
Asked for information to share with prospects about the upcoming Gong integration; told PMM enablement content is currently in progress.

Escalated Routeware account had Kaia failing to auto-join/record Zoom meetings; root-caused to Zoom admin+user-level auth not yet supporting live ingestion feature flags (Jira VI-15193), with a related Varonis case surfacing a separate Zoom local-recording-privilege issue.
Asked for additional best-practice resources on content card triggers to share with a client; pointed to a relevant support article.
Sought a subject matter expert on O365 environment technical requirements for a Kaia expansion; awaiting customer's IT clarification before further guidance.
Asked via /kaiaq about the differences between Kaia for Voice and a full Kaia license; clarified Engage-only users get post-call processing but no live experience, content cards, or coach cards.

Asked whether AI Topics Explorer content is configurable for Vector Solutions' compliance/privacy-concern use case; told the current version isn't configurable but a configurability capability is planned in roughly 3-4 months.

Asked whether Kaia can record a Teams meeting hosted by an outside client (SailPoint use case); confirmed no native support, with workarounds being obtaining the host's cloud recording or an alternate solution carrying noted risk.

A customer asked whether the full transcript (not just the summary) can be shared alongside a Kaia recording; confirmed not currently supported, though a full download link to the recording does include the transcript.

Follow-up confirming there's no option to include the full transcript when sharing a Kaia recording (only the meeting summary), flagged as a possible future feature; transcript-based closed captions raised as a separate accessibility consideration.
A user at Avis Budget with correct Kaia/consent/meet settings still can't get Kaia to join meetings on Zoom or Teams.
Reported Varonis Zoom meetings joining but not recording; resolved via cross-reference to the Routeware thread, with root cause being some users needing to enable Zoom local recording privileges.
Positive feedback on the new ability to upload calls directly to Kaia.

Asked whether Outreach's Twilio call routing uses a France server for Barcelona-dialed calls, relevant to a churned prospect's SalesLoft/Twilio call-quality issue; confirmed EU calls route through Ireland or Germany, not France.
Reported repeated notification emails for calls already auto-scored by AI coaching; engineering identified and deployed a fix that stopped the re-scoring loop on the reported calls.
Asked what IP addresses a customer should whitelist for their SFTP server receiving Kaia daily exports; confirmed there's no fixed IP list since export traffic runs on Azure outside Bento.
Sales asked whether there are plans to integrate Five9 Dialer data into Kaia for an in-progress deal.

An in-person recording failed to upload/show in the mobile app ahead of a critical FreshWorks eval; identified as a known bug tied to an outdated mobile app version, resolved by updating to the latest app version (1.9.3).

Requested a getting-started implementation guide for a client with full platform access who has never used Kaia; existing support articles were seen as insufficient, and a colleague offered to follow up directly with tailored guidance.
Asked via /kaiaq whether an API exists to check many users' Kaia auto-join settings in bulk; bot response indicated no official API currently exists for this.

Asked if Clari Copilot recording ingestion is on the roadmap alongside Gong; confirmed Gong ingestion is in private preview, Clari wasn't planned but migration tooling could be extended if a customer candidate emerges.

Asked via /kaiaq for likely causes when Kaia fails to auto-associate a recording with the right Prospect/Account/Opportunity; bot listed opportunity timing, prospect-to-opportunity linkage, and calendar/scheduling-link issues as common causes.

Discussed best practice for configuring Kaia vocabulary terms for acronyms like NVD; clarified vocab entries should be based on observed mis-transcriptions rather than proactively guessed, informing a vocab-term generator tool in development.

Asked whether Kaia data (specifically coaching scorecards) would be exposed via MCP for use in Claude; discussion confirmed coach cards weren't yet exposed via MCP, resulting in Jira VI-15258 to add scorecard search/fetch tools.

SAP team asked whether Kaia recording visibility permissions can be split by Voice vs. Meeting format for Managers; confirmed no such separation exists, recommending a narrower 'owned by them and their reports' permission scope as an adoption-friendly interim approach.

Motive hit a Salesforce field-mapping error configuring the Kaia Recording CRM object due to a known Flagship/GQL API call-routing bug; engineering merged and deployed a fix, and Motive confirmed the remapping worked afterward.
Bizagi asked about vague company-details requirements for purchasing a South African phone number; routed to the Voice team/channel for specialist guidance.

requester_role: Senior Director, GTM AI Advisory Services
summary: Asked via /kaiaq whether Kaia auto-join can be prevented by domain; bot response indicated no direct support for domain-based join restrictions currently exists.

requester_role: Senior Director, GTM AI Advisory Services
summary: HighRadius reported Kaia joining internal same-domain calls because consent pages were enabled on all their conferencing providers; Outreach explained internal meetings must be scheduled without a consent link and redirected the team to the videoconferencing-consent channel for the scheduling workaround.

While setting up a Google Meet customer, the connect option wasn't visible while impersonating a user; resolved by explaining that provider connection status isn't shown under impersonation and should be checked via Kaia settings > user connections or by the end user directly.

Follow-up asking how to enable the Google Meet connection at the user level; clarified this is expected behavior under impersonation and each user must authorize Google Meet themselves in their own personal settings.

Asked whether a customer needing only Kaia for Voice transcripts via API also needs a conferencing provider configured; confirmed API access isn't license-gated and only requires that recordings with transcripts exist.

Waystar disabled Zoom's local-recording permission over 'bad actor' security concerns, which blocked Kaia from recording/transcribing and thus generating summaries; Outreach explained the dependency and also flagged a likely bug where summary emails are still sent for meetings with no actual recording.

Spectrum, running a Kaia/Amplify pilot, asked whether upcoming feature-release enhancements would be visible only to pilot users or the whole org; the question was outside Kaia's scope and redirected to the general outreach-questions channel, unanswered in this thread.

Internal call-to-action to identify Gong-using customers who could pilot the Amplify SKU via a Gong integration beta; multiple candidate accounts (Perk, Braze, Solarwinds, Tebra, WalkMe) were surfaced and routed to a dedicated private beta channel for enrollment.

Ahead of a FreshWorks Amplify pilot, asked about Topics Explorer pricing/credit consumption and Meeting Prep agent cost; confirmed Topics Explorer currently doesn't consume Amplify credits while Meeting Prep costs 2 credits per brief, with future Topics Explorer monetization still undecided.

Bottomline wasn't seeing AI-suggested responses on a custom coach card; resolved by pointing to a per-question setting in the Coach Card configuration, and confirmed suggested answers require only Meet (not Amplify) while auto-scoring requires Amplify.

Asked whether meetings can still be deleted from the Kaia meeting (detail) view since that option seemed to have disappeared; confirmed deletion is still available from the Recordings list view, though the in-meeting-view option is gone.

Databricks reported Google Calendar meeting links changing shortly before meetings, causing host/guest link mismatches, and speculated Kaia's calendar sync was rewriting event data; Outreach clarified Kaia only reads events via the official Google Meet SDK and doesn't rewrite them, and traced the affected user's issue to a disconnected calendar.

Reported being unable to submit notes or view a Ramp call recording in the UI right after the meeting ended; self-resolved once the recording finished processing (it just took longer than usual to appear).

Asked via /kaiaq what defines a 'reviewed' call in the coaching metrics dashboard; the bot gave a general, non-definitive answer pointing to Team Activity Report documentation without a precise definition.

Asked for a way to exclude Kaia auto-join for meetings with specific external email domains so sellers don't have to manually opt out each time; told that auto-join already skips meetings where an excluded contact is on the invite.

Asked via /kaiaq whether Kaia recovers a recording if a user leaves and rejoins a Zoom meeting; the bot confirmed Kaia does not stitch recordings together and instead produces two separate recordings.

A 39-minute meeting was cut off with only 10 minutes recorded, tied to a FAILED_PRECONDITION error in Datadog logs; Outreach explained Kaia doesn't auto-rejoin after being kicked and requires 'Join Meeting with Kaia', but the missing first portion of the recording (before the user's rejoin) remained unresolved in-thread.
Lyft reported that Kaia meeting recordings stopped mid-call without any host action in two instances.
Asked what counts as a recording being 'played' (click vs. partial vs. full watch); confirmed that clicking play alone is enough to count as watched.
Asked via /kaiaq how to get Kaia into an unscheduled Zoom meeting; the bot answered to use the 'Join Meeting with Kaia' option for ad-hoc joins.

A US-only Kaia customer expanding to EMEA had regulatory concerns; received a full breakdown of platform-specific consent configurations (Teams, Zoom, Google Meet, Voice) and EU data residency/GDPR options for staying compliant in the region.

Amex, already escalated over deleted prospects removing call data, asked for visibility into who deletes Kaia meetings; audit logs technically capture deletes as 'update' events with deleted:true but lack an easy Bulk Actions/reporting surface, so a separate feature request is being filed for proper delete-visibility reporting.

Asked how to pause Kaia recording mid-meeting on MS Teams; clarified there's no pause and the correct way to bring Kaia back mid-call is the 'Join Meeting with Kaia' button (not the generic add-Kaia surface), which preserves calendar/CRM linkage, though neither button appears when a consent page is enabled.

Asked why posting live notes during Kaia meetings had become inconsistent after returning from leave; explained the old 'Notes' feature was retired and replaced by a richer live in-call/transcript @mention Comments experience.

Clarified whether Kaia can be manually added to a non-user-hosted client meeting on Zoom vs. Teams for SailPoint; confirmed Zoom allows it (with proper host-tenant permissions) but Teams' security model blocks bringing an external bot into another org's meeting, and flagged SailPoint's low Kaia adoption due to their RSC Teams deployment.

A customer evaluating Kaia as a Gong replacement asked whether historical tracker/topic-mention data would be lost on migration; confirmed Gong trackers aren't migrated but Smart Topics get an automatic 30-day historical backfill on creation, with a longer backfill possible via a PS engagement.

requester_role: Senior Manager, GTM AI Advisory Services
summary: Subsplash's IT team needed specifics (AWS account ID, region, file structure, encryption) to configure an S3 bucket for the Kaia bulk export; clarified the export doesn't use AWS identity (originates from Azure) and the customer instead needs to grant blanket bucket access per the daily-export documentation.

Asked whether MS Teams admin approval alone is sufficient for Kaia to work, or whether per-user assignment is also required; clarified this depends on RSC vs. non-RSC deployment (RSC requires app assignment to users; Bay Cities' non-RSC/admin-consent deployment has no end-user requirement).

A customer was approached by Zoom to buy out their Kaia contract with a competing Conversation Intelligence offering; the internal team compared feature gaps (weaker in-person voice-diarization/consent handling, English-only stats) to arm the rep with a competitive response.

Confirmed for HighRadius that Kaia meeting-summary recap emails only go to meeting participants recognized as signed-in Outreach users in the host's org, regardless of Meet license, per the FAQ, noting a recent change may have somewhat broadened recipient recognition.

Clarified for a customer wanting Kaia data in Power BI that Snowflake Data Share doesn't yet expose Kaia transcripts (only API or daily export do), that API access requires no special enablement, and connected the requester with the API team for a step-by-step setup guide.

Asked whether HighRadius users logging into MS Teams via their onmicrosoft.com fallback domain would prevent Kaia from joining; confirmed domain doesn't matter for the admin-only Teams deployment, but surfaced several unmapped Outreach-to-Teams user accounts plus low Google Meet/Webex setup adoption needing admin remediation.
Internal user asked how long a manually uploaded Zoom recording takes to process in Kaia and where to find it, after not getting the completion email; it finally notified after about two hours.

Asked whether an in-person meeting recorded via the Outreach app is expected to show as "Uploaded file" source; engineering confirmed it is current behavior but agreed the label/tagging needs to be improved to be findable.

Asked about mobile in-person recording processing time and reported a stuck/failed upload for a Lyft user; engineering traced it to a known mobile app bug where failed uploads weren't handled properly and recommended re-uploading.
Asked whether a newly created custom topic retroactively appears in Kaia topic reporting; confirmed a 30-day backfill applies with the option to extend further by scoping the request.

Amex requested a report of who deleted Kaia meetings, the file name, and when; team found the deletion event type in the data warehouse but hit limitations getting the deleting user and isolating delete-only events from audit logs.

Reported that the Amount field on the Kaia page wasn't populating; root cause was the UI only rendering Amount when currencyType was also present (which is often null), and engineering shipped a fix to render Amount regardless.

A manually uploaded Zoom recording had jumbled/incorrect speaker splits after Kaia failed to auto-join or force-join the meeting, requiring reliance on the raw Zoom recording; engineering flagged this join failure as a bug to investigate and requested logs while another team member reported a similar diarization issue.

During ServiceNow's Outreach org migration, asked whether connecting Kaia to MS Teams in the new instance creates a separate Teams app; confirmed two Outreach orgs on the same MS tenant share the same Kaia app, though duplicate Kaia bots can appear if a meeting syncs to both orgs.

Asked what an Engage+Meet customer already gets vs. needs Amplify for (AI Topics Explorer and Smart Kaia Coach auto-scoring); confirmed Amplify+Meet is required for AI Topics Explorer and for AI auto-scoring of coaching cards, while regular coach cards and AI-suggested scores are included with Engage and Meet.

Asked whether Kaia meeting summaries push back into Salesforce in Outreach's own instance; confirmed it currently doesn't (Rally uses an older Description-field method) and discussed recommending the newer CRM object-based summary sync instead, with an action item to deprecate the old approach.
Asked if Kaia call summary notes can be pushed into Salesforce for Ericsson; confirmed yes and shared the support article for configuring the Kaia recording CRM object.

Reported a customer getting "An unexpected error occurred" when downloading a Kaia voice call; support asked for org ID, user ID, and recording link to investigate further (no resolution captured in thread).

McKesson asked for Meeting Type to be added as a column (not just a filter) on the Kaia home page; product confirmed no current plans but that it's feasible, and the requester logged it as a feature request.

Asked whether deleting a Kaia call/transcript also triggers deletion in Snowflake for customers with data sharing; confirmed it should, with a noted upcoming change to retain some IDs while marking records deleted.

Flagged a malformed-record parsing failure in the kaia_meeting_events Clerk CDC table; traced to bad timestamps in a Chorus-imported recording's utterances, with a fix in progress to skip/guard such bad records on import.

Asked if Kaia can support both Zoom and Teams for one org, believing only one provider was allowed; clarified that a Meet-licensed org can actually use all available providers, and flagged the support article stating otherwise as outdated.

During a high-value DoorDash Kaia pilot (Gong compete), the live transcript did not display during a Zoom meeting though it was captured post-processing; engineering explained live-experience socket events are fire-and-forget/best-effort and asked the client to retest.

Asked how to filter Kaia recordings to exclude no-show/internal-only meetings so a customer can count prospect meetings accurately; confirmed no such filter exists today (logged as a feature request) since internal/external attendee resolution isn't precise.
/kaiaq bot question on which cloud provider stores Kaia recordings, transcripts, and AI summaries; bot answered Azure, with TLS in transit and Azure CosmosDB/Storage encryption at rest.

SailPoint could not pull Topics data through the API because Topics were only supported on single-recording API requests, not list requests; engineering added and deployed topics support to the list recordings API and confirmed it working for the customer.
An Outreach employee reported Kaia no longer joining their Zoom calls despite correct auto-join settings, after previously hitting a local-recording config error.

/kaiaq bot question on whether the Kaia transcript is available via API; bot cited daily bulk exports/listener licenses as alternatives, and a team member clarified the API returns a link to the transcript JSON rather than raw text.

Subsplash wanted to set up Kaia Daily Export to S3 using AWS IAM roles instead of a static access key/secret for security reasons; confirmed Outreach only supports static IAM user credentials today, discussed API/Snowflake data-sharing alternatives, and the cross-account IAM role request was logged as a feature request to route through product.
Asked whether local-machine recording permission is still required for Kaia to record Zoom meetings; confirmed it's a Zoom-side requirement that has not been removed.

A customer (identified only by org GUID) hit an error saving credentials while setting up daily Kaia export; Datadog logs showed their IAM user was missing required permissions, and the support article listing required permissions was shared to resolve it.

Reported a Zoom recording uploaded to Rally never appeared after days with no error visibility, suggesting better upload error surfacing; a teammate confirmed the meeting was actually present in the Rally org.

MarginEdge reported Kaia speaker diarization on Google Meet was wrong 20-50% of the time, mostly on short back-and-forth turns; confirmed diarization is gain-signal based on Google's data and that a new diarization technique is actively being worked on, with customer examples used to help prioritize fixes.
Asked whether customers can get more than 9 languages for Kaia transcription; confirmed it requires a feature request, which the requester then submitted as an SFDC case.

Customer's "Add Kaia to live call" button was grayed out on MS Teams; confirmed this is by design because the customer has the recording consent page enabled, which forces Kaia to auto-join via consent links only and disables manual add to prevent bypassing consent.
Data engineering asked whether a Kaia transcript table in Databricks contains PHI/PII as part of a HIPAA-compliance effort.

Requested an expert join a call with a customer trialing 11 Kaia licenses (evaluating Gong, no paid PS) to help resolve configuration problems and demonstrate value during the 3-week trial; an engineer offered to help asynchronously and later agreed to join a later call time.

/kaiaq bot question on which Zoom APIs, permissions, and account-level settings Kaia depends on to record meetings; bot detailed the Zoom Meeting Bots SDK, Zoom Admin App installation, local recording, and host/participant consent requirements.
A customer trying to add Kaia to an Outlook-booked meeting gets a 'video consent not enabled' error.

TJ asked what's required for Kaia and the deal agent to populate the Next Steps Opportunity field; the bot explained the Opportunity must exist before the meeting and have a linked prospect for the association to work.

Brad asked whether Kaia processes voice data for speaker identification; confirmed Kaia uses conference signals (not biometrics) to diarize transcripts, with accuracy depending on availability of provider transcripts.

Ricky asked for documentation on managing recording consent outside of Kaia via conference provider tools; answered that only Zoom has proper consent management and Outreach doesn't collect or track third-party consent documents.

Tony asked for the pros/cons of letting a customer use Gong for call insights alongside Kaia and when that capability would go live; Bogdan noted Outreach is cheaper for CI but Gong has invested far more in CI, though returns are diminishing as agentic workflows shift back to raw transcripts.

Rakesh asked how to access the Zoom chat transcript or the Zoom recording link from a Kaia-recorded meeting; answered that Kaia doesn't capture Zoom chat content and provides no way to retrieve the associated Zoom recording link.

Javi asked how long the Kaia bot waits before leaving a Google Meet call if not admitted and requested extending the 60-second timeout; engineering confirmed there's no waiting room (bot leaves 60s after the inviting user joins) and the timeout can't be changed since it's imposed by Google.

Cara saw a warning message when Kaia joined a Zoom call that Zoom was also recording; team explained a Zoom local-recording permission must be enabled for Kaia to record as a participant, confirmed this applies to customers using Zoom consent too, and pointed to a manual recording-upload workaround.

Tony asked whether Kaia could ingest MindTickle call data via MCP (or run alongside a MindTickle recorder) to help win a $500K Navex deal where the customer won't give up MindTickle CI; team confirmed no current integration exists, MindTickle is building its own Kaia integration, and partner team could only estimate a Q4 timeline.

Beckie asked if the Kaia mobile app can distinguish speakers in in-person meeting recordings; confirmed it can separate speakers but can't automatically identify who is who, requiring a few manual clicks to label them.

Javi asked if custom KAIA content card types and content-card governance (team/role targeting) had been considered, since these come up consistently with customers; Bogdan said neither is on the roadmap but encouraged filing a formal feature request.

DigitalOcean reported that Google Meet participants could only join as viewers (no mic/camera) when Kaia's consent bot was present; engineering determined this is a Google-imposed restriction for outdated/incompatible devices joining after the bot, unrelated to consent, with a workaround of using Google's native cloud recording instead.

An unnamed customer asked whether the "Start Outreach Kaia" button reappears after it disappears in Google Meet; Bogdan explained the bot times out if not admitted but can be re-triggered via "Join Meeting with Kaia," and that any member of the host org (regardless of Kaia license) can admit it.

Cohesity's Kaia transcript export summary email went to a long list of recipients beyond admins; investigation found most were current or inactive admins plus the person running the ad hoc export, but Xiomara flagged that inactive admins shouldn't have been emailed, and the thread ended without full resolution.

Siemens asked whether the email notification sent when a Kaia/Orchestrate license is assigned can be suppressed; confirmed there's currently no way to suppress it (a possible FR), with a guessed workaround of toggling the Teams provider off/on around bulk license allocation.

MSCI's security team required detailed justification for every Microsoft Graph/Teams permission Kaia requests (data handling, retention, revocability) before approving production deployment; engineering provided a permissions one-pager and joined a customer call, clarifying that AppCatalog permissions are removable post-onboarding while TeamsAppInstallation and offline-access scopes are required for Kaia to keep functioning.

TJ asked if coach cards could be triggered by call type/workflow rather than just audio cues for more targeted real-time coaching; Bogdan clarified that's not a current feature but a "guided conversation" capability is in development, starting with AMEX.

MarginEdge, having just migrated from Gong to Outreach, gave enthusiastic positive feedback that Kaia's call analysis was more accurate than Gong's; the team discussed turning it into a customer case study/marketing story.

Kaia failed to join a Medius Teams meeting; investigation found several Medius users had invalid Teams OAuth tokens needing re-authorization, and the thread also surfaced a broader "meeting isn't owned by the org" issue caused by a 30-second Graph API validation timeout for orgs with many meetings (also seen at Hearst Newspapers), which engineering planned to fix via parallelized validation.

A Lyft rep's meeting was missing the "Join Meeting with Kaia" button; investigation pointed to either a calendar-sync timing delay or the rep not being logged into Outreach, but no conclusive root cause could be confirmed from the available logs.

Rick asked if external transcripts (e.g., from Teams) can be uploaded into Kaia; confirmed transcripts can't be uploaded directly, but recordings can be manually uploaded or auto-ingested via the Teams RSC cloud-recording flow.

A Sailpoint user with auto-join set to "Always" had a call Kaia didn't join automatically; Bogdan asked for the specific meeting details to investigate, and the thread ended without a confirmed root cause.

requester_role: Senior Manager, GTM AI Advisory Services
summary: Customer Vector wants to query coaching-card completion/topic data through the Kaia MCP/Claude connection (e.g., "who's done their coaching cards this week"); the request was routed to the mcp-public channel and product team to consider adding such query tools to a future MCP release.
Natalya asked whether per-user auto-join settings could be pulled from Databricks for a client report; Bogdan confirmed that's not possible.
A Kaia meeting summary was missing from the internal sales instance; Bogdan manually triggered generation and noted the automatic recovery pipeline had failed to regenerate it on its own.

After Onfido was acquired by Entrust, Kaia kept surfacing Entrust as a competitor on calls; the team confirmed there's currently no way to retrain this (custom topics and docknowledge won't help) and that a future "Org Context" feature, not yet available, would be needed to fix it.

Databricks reps using Zoom's post-recording consent flow wanted to know if they're notified when a prospect declines recording consent; Bogdan said that's entirely governed by Zoom's own settings, outside Outreach's control, and the customer should work directly with Zoom support.

Petr flagged that oracle-consume-smartworker was failing with "Org unavailable due to org state" for a paused test org move, likely because a draining phase was missed; engineers discussed how to respect org-lifecycle events in the CDC handler and moved further debugging to a dedicated channel.

TJ asked how Kaia handles recording consent in two-party consent states; the bot explained platform-specific handling (Zoom native consent, Teams via admin settings/logs, Outreach Voice's own consent dialog), with Bogdan noting the Voice details should be confirmed with the voice team.

TJ asked whether Kaia needs to be on every call and how to customize when it shows up; the bot explained auto-join is driven by host license, external-attendee requirements on platforms like Google Meet, and admin-configurable rules/filters.
